newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Peseta debt/interbank market closing report.

text.p: The Spanish debt market ended down on Thursday, as by French Prime Minister Lionel Jospin comments on French public finances prompted a technical correction downward, dealers said.
"It's not serious. I would rule out any correction below the 116.00 (for long bond future)," a dealer said.
He added that domestic investors were supporting bonos.
"We saw domestic investment trusts buying on the dip just before the close on the five year maturity," he said.
The 10-year spread over Bunds ended wider at 65 basis points from 60 basis points this morning.
"Domestic investors still collect a lot of money and so they have to invest it, no matter the uncertainty over EMU," said a dealer in Madrid.
The short-end of the yield curve could benefit from expectations for another official rate cut by the Bank of Spain.

"The market is divided (on the possibility of a rate cut next Tuesday)," a dealer said. "I'm more with the ones expecting a 25 basis points cut, but I have to admit there's only a 50 percent probability," he added.
